chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was asked about a woman who has a husband, and his intellect has been affected after he married her, or insanity befalls him. He said to her: 'She may remove herself from him if she wishes.'

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a wife if her husband becomes insane after marriage?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the Chapter of *Al-Li'an*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the wife's unilateral right to initiate separation (*tanzi' nafsaha*) if her husband becomes insane after marriage. This ruling highlights the juristic principle that mental soundness is a fundamental condition for the stability of the marital bond, granting the wife autonomy without requiring a formal court decree for the dissolution to be valid in this specific context.
